**No.** Most characters get enough depth to feel human. Carl has a backstory (his mother left), a real failing, and a later, more genuine apology. Martin's self-aware interpretive habit softens into honesty when he admits he disguised interest as concern. Lizzy moves from witty commentator to someone with her own wound, the unspoken love back home, and her own slow, conditional forgiveness.

Johan is the exception. He stays an idealized, flawless figure who simply "sees" Mara without judgment. His traits (from Helsinki, has a sister) are mentioned but never explored. He has no weaknesses, desires, or changes of his own. He works mainly as a thematic foil and a resolution device, the "right" kind of attention set against Carl's and Martin's. So he reads as present to fulfill a structural need rather than as a fully realized person.
